name: SpikeHeightMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: a strong breakout has at least a 60 percent chance of reaching a measured move that is approximately equal to the size of the spike
description: After a with-trend breakout spike, project a target beyond the breakout point equal to the height of the spike that produced it; exit (or take partial profits on) the long when the high reaches it.
pseudocode: spikeLow = lowest(low, spikeLookback)[b]; spikeHigh = high[b]; target = breakoutPoint + (spikeHigh - spikeLow); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: target is frozen at the breakout bar; a lowest-low window otherwise

notes: Same construction as chapter 8's TradingRangeHeightTarget/SpikeHeightMeasuredMove (R08-13/R08-22); the dedup pass should merge these families.

name: BearBarInBullTrendFirstTarget
quote: Their first target was a move to the high of the bar, which occurred two bars later
description: After buying the close of a bear bar per RP1-08, the first exit target is that same bar's high.
pseudocode: entryBarHigh = high[e]; high[0] >= entryBarHigh - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the entry bar's high

complexity.reason: the entry bar's high must persist as remembered state across subsequent bars

name: BearBarInBullTrendMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: the next target is a measured move up, equal to the height of the bear trend bar
description: Second exit target after RP1-09: project the height of the bear entry bar above its own high.

book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: target is frozen from the entry bar's own range

name: GapMidpointOrFirstLegHighMeasuredMove
quote: The low of the bar after the breakout bar and the high of the bar 11 breakout point created a breakout gap. Either its middle or the high of the first leg up to bar 11 could lead to a measured move up.
description: After a breakout gap forms, project a measured move from whichever of two anchors is nearer — the gap's midpoint or the high of the first leg up to the breakout — and exit when price reaches it.
pseudocode: gapMid = (low[b + 1] + high[b]) / 2; anchor = min(gapMid, legHigh); target = anchor + (anchor - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: needs the breakout bar, the first-leg high, and the leg start all remembered as state

notes: Same family as RP1-07 and chapter 8's measured-move targets (R08-05/09/10); the dedup pass should merge.

name: ScalpProfitNotAchievedBeforePullback
quote: A trader who bought on a stop above a prior swing high would not be able to make a scalper's profit before there was a pullback.
description: Sign of weakness: price never travels far enough beyond the swing-high breakout to reach a scalp target before pulling back (mirrors R02-06's strength sign).
pseudocode: swingHigh = highest(high, swingLookback)[1]; highest(high, pullbackWindow) - swingHigh < scalpTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: n/a (breakout-failure signal)

complexity.reason: needs a forward-looking window evaluated once the pullback is identified

name: SpikeMeasuredMoveOpenToClose
quote: When a breakout is that strong, it usually is followed by a channel and often leads to a measured move from the open of the first bar to the close of the final bar in the spike.
description: After a strong spike from bar s to bar e, project a measured move using the spike's open-to-close height (rather than its high-low range) added beyond the spike's close.
pseudocode: height = close[e] - open[s]; target = close[e] + height; high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: the spike's start and end bars must persist as remembered state

notes: Distinct anchor from RP1-07/R08's high-low spike height; the dedup pass should keep both forms since Brooks uses each in different places.

name: MultipleMeasuredMoveTargetsWatchNearest
quote: there are usually several possibilities for the measurement points and it is best to watch the nearest target first ... Once that measured move was exceeded, traders should look at other possibilities.
description: When several measured-move candidates (open-to-close, open-to-high, low-to-close, low-to-high of the spike, all projected forward) are in play, take profits at whichever untouched target is nearest, then move on to the next one.
pseudocode: targets = { openToCloseTarget, openToHighTarget, lowToCloseTarget, lowToHighTarget }; nearestUntouched = min(t in targets where t > close[0]); high[0] >= nearestUntouched - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at each successive projection

complexity.reason: requires computing and ranking several measured-move anchors simultaneously and tracking which have already been reached

notes: Ties together RP1-07, R02-34 and other single-anchor measured-move candidates as alternative targets rather than one fixed target.

name: WedgeMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: The market tried to form a wedge bear flag beginning at the bar 4 low, and it had three pushes up ... Using the bar 4 low to the top of the wedge for the measurement projected a move that was exceeded by only one tick at the bar 14 high of the day.
description: After a failed three-push wedge, project a measured move from the wedge's start low to its top, added again above the top.
pseudocode: wedgeStart = low[s]; wedgeTop = highest(high, wedgeBars)[e]; target = wedgeTop + (wedgeTop - wedgeStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: needs three-push wedge recognition and remembered start/top levels

notes: Related to R02-37's three-push channel primitive.

name: MovingAverageScalpTarget
quote: Another common gap is between the high or low of a bar and the moving average. In trends, these can set up good swing trades that test the extreme of the trend, and in trading ranges, they often set up scalps to the moving average.
description: Exit/take profit on a scalp position when price reaches the EMA.
pseudocode: high[0] >= ema(emaLength) - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the moving average

complexity.reason: needs the EMA value each bar

name: TakeProfitAtInitialRiskMultiple
quote: the reward has to be at least as large as the risk to create a positive trader's equation. This usually results in some profit taking once the reward reaches the size of the risk
description: Take (partial) profits once open profit reaches at least riskMultiple times the position's initial risk (entry price minus the initial protective stop).
pseudocode: initialRisk = abs(ctx.EntryPrice() - ctx.InitialStopPrice()); ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= riskMultiple * initialRisk
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at 1R (or riskMultiple x R)

complexity.reason: needs the position's initial stop distance remembered, not just a fixed dollar amount like TakeProfit

notes: Unlike TakeProfitWithRatioStop (fixed dollar target with a stop expressed as a ratio of it), this scales the profit target off the trade's own actual initial risk, which varies by placement.

name: SpikeOpenToCloseMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: The open of the first bar was eight points below the close of the third and final bull trend bar in the spike, so the spike should be thought of as being eight points tall, at a minimum... take the number of points from the open of the first bar of the spike to the close of the final bar of the spike and add that to the close of that final bar of the spike.
description: Primary measured-move formula: spikeHeight = close[lastSpikeBar] - open[firstSpikeBar]; target = close[lastSpikeBar] + spikeHeight; take profit on the long when price reaches it.
pseudocode: spikeHeight = close[lastSpikeBar] - open[firstSpikeBar]; target = close[lastSpikeBar] + spikeHeight; high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: the spike's start/end bars must persist once identified; the arithmetic itself is trivial

notes: Distinct from R08-22's SpikeHeightMeasuredMove, which used high[end]-low[start]; this chapter's primary reference points are open-of-first to close-of-last. Dedup pass should compare/merge the family.

name: ChannelBottomRetestAfterMeasuredMove
quote: The market invariably overshoots and has to backtrack to home in on a 50-50 market. The measured move area is an overshoot of the odds, and they then briefly favor the bears. Once the market retraces to the bottom of the channel, the odds again overshoot, but this time in favor of the bulls.
description: After price reaches the spike/channel measured-move target (R07-05) and reverses, project the correction's target at the bottom of the channel that followed the spike; this is both a place to expect support and a re-entry area for the trend.
pseudocode: channelBottom = lowest(low, channelBars); low[0] <= channelBottom + toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: buy near the bottom of the channel (re-entry) or cover a countertrend short there

complexity.reason: needs a remembered channel-bottom level in addition to the already-tracked measured-move target

name: Leg1EqualsLeg2MeasuredMoveTarget
quote: When a market makes a sharp move and then has a pullback, it will likely have a second leg and the second leg is frequently approximately the same size as the first. This is a leg 1 = leg 2 move, but it is also called an ABC move or an AB = CD... for the AB = CD in a bull trend, if you start at point A and add the length of the AB leg (which is B - A), then add that to C, you get C + (B - A).
description: The classic leg-1-equals-leg-2 (AB=CD) measured move: given swing points A (leg 1 start), B (leg 1 end), C (pullback end/leg 2 start), target D = C + (B - A); take profit on the long when price reaches D.
pseudocode: A = mostRecentSwingLow(pivotStrength, lookback)[2]; B = mostRecentSwingHigh(pivotStrength, lookback)[1]; C = mostRecentSwingLow(pivotStrength, lookback); target = C + (B - A); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection; countertrend setups may also be considered near it

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection for three points (A, B, C), the canonical measured-move construction this chapter is named for

notes: Brooks explicitly rejects the confusing ABCD/AB=CD alphabetical labeling in favor of 'leg 1 / pullback / leg 2'; kept here under the simpler name.

Mathematically identical to computing the target from the pullback's midpoint (the 'thick area' argument, p71-72): C + (B-A) = thickAreaMid + (thickAreaMid - A) when C is the pullback's low and thickAreaMid = (B+C)/2 is not generally equal, but the book shows both formulas resolve to C + (B-A); the thick-area version is not separately encoded since it is the same target.

name: NestedLegMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: a trader could look at AD as a first leg that contains two smaller legs (AB and CD), and then stay long until there was a measured move up (AD = EF, and the target is the top of the solid line).
description: Apply the leg-1-equals-leg-2 construction one level up: treat an entire two-legged move (A to D, itself made of smaller legs AB and CD) as the new 'leg 1', and project an equal move E-to-F after the next pullback (E).
pseudocode: legHeight = D - A; target = E + legHeight; high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the larger-scale projection

complexity.reason: same swing-pivot dependency as R07-07 but one scale up, requiring a hierarchy of pivots (A,B,C,D,E)

chapter_title: Measured Moves Based on the Size of the First Leg (the Spike)

name: TradingRangeMidpointMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: When a market has a strong trend move and then a fairly strong pullback leg, and then a trading range, traders can use the approximate middle of the range to project where the second leg of the pullback might reach. As the trading range unfolds, keep adjusting the line to where you estimate the midpoint is, and that will usually be around the midpoint of the pullback once the move has finally completed its second leg.
description: While a pullback trading range is still developing, continuously project target = 2 x rangeMidpoint - pullbackStart, updating rangeMidpoint each bar as the range's own highest-high/lowest-low midpoint (equivalent to a leg-1=leg-2 measured move using a moving estimate of point C).
pseudocode: rangeMidpoint = (highest(high, rangeBars) + lowest(low, rangeBars)) / 2; target = 2 * rangeMidpoint - pullbackStart; high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection, continuously re-estimated

complexity.reason: the target is recomputed every bar from a rolling window rather than fixed once at a detected pivot

notes: Figure 7.3's worked example.

name: AmbiguousLegStartMultipleTargetsFilter
quote: astute traders were open to the possibility that the correction up to bar 9 began at bar 4 and not bar 6, and therefore thought that the second leg down might be equal to the bar 1 to bar 4 first leg down instead of the bar 1 to bar 6 first leg down.
description: When the true start of leg 1 is ambiguous among multiple plausible swing points, compute a leg-1=leg-2 target from each candidate start and watch all of them, rather than committing to a single measured move.
pseudocode: targets = [C + (B - candidateA_i) for candidateA_i in plausibleLegStarts]; for each target, test high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks*tickSize
book_order_type: n/a (target-selection heuristic feeding R07-07)

complexity.reason: choosing which swing points are 'plausible' candidate leg starts is itself a design decision, not a mechanical test

notes: Figure 7.2's worked example; the book also raises an Elliott Wave 'flat' interpretation for this ambiguity, which is not itself mechanizable (see rejected).

name: GapMidpointMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: Traders measured from the bar 1 bottom of the rally to the middle of the gap and then projected that same number of points upward.
description: After a gap-up bar g, gapMid = (low[g] + high[g+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest low over legLookback bars ending at g; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart). Exit the long when the high reaches the target within a tolerance.
pseudocode: gapMid = (low[g] + high[g+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest(low, legLookback)[g]; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection

complexity.reason: target persists from a detected gap bar and needs the start of the leg that contains it

notes: Emini traders regard a target as tested only within one tick (p76); toleranceTicks encodes that.
Brooks: look at the nearest target first (p77).

name: CountertrendOnlyAtMeasuredMove
quote: The key is to trade only with the trend, but once the market is in the area of the measured move, you can begin to look for countertrend entries.
description: Filter for countertrend (short) entries in a bull leg: permit them only once the high has reached the measured-move target area.
pseudocode: high[0] >= target - nearTargetAtr * atr(atrLookback)
book_order_type: n/a (gate on countertrend entries)

complexity.reason: depends on a measured-move target

name: SpikeHeightMeasuredMove
quote: The five-bar spike down to bar 13 led to a measured move down, and the low of the day missed it by a tick.
description: After a spike of N consecutive bull trend bars ending at bar e and starting at bar s, target = high[e] + (high[e] - low[s]); exit long when the high reaches it.
pseudocode: spike = consecutiveBullTrendBars >= spikeBars; target = high[e] + (high[e] - low[s]); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

name: LateSessionMeasuredMoveUnlikely
quote: it was so late in the day that a measured move from its midpoint was unlikely to be reached.
description: Filter: do not initiate a measured-move swing when fewer than N bars remain in the session.
pseudocode: barsRemainingInSession(sessionEndTime) >= minBarsRemaining
book_order_type: n/a (time filter)

complexity.reason: needs bar time and session end

name: FixedTickOrDollarProfitTarget
quote: Common profit targets for scalp and swing positions: in AAPL, 50 cents and a dollar; in the 5 minute Emini, five to six ticks for a four-tick scalp, and three, four, and 10 points for a swing.
description: Exit when open profit reaches a fixed tick/dollar amount -- a small target for a scalp, a larger one for a swing.
pseudocode: ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= targetDollars
book_order_type: limit order at the fixed target

name: MinimumRewardToRiskFilter
quote: Once they determine their risk, they can then set a profit target that is at least as large as the risk and reasonably assume that they have about a 60 percent chance or better of being successful.
description: Filter: only take a signal if its planned reward (distance from entry to target) is at least a multiple of its planned risk (distance from entry to protective stop).

book_order_type: n/a (trade-selection filter, applied before placing the entry order)

name: ExitOnSecondWithTrendResumptionAttemptFailure
quote: one of the cardinal rules about trading reversals is to exit on the market's second attempt to resume the trend.
description: Exit a position held in the old trend direction once the market's second attempt to resume that trend fails (e.g. a second high-2/low-2-style resumption attempt is rejected), since a second failed attempt raises the odds the trend has genuinely reversed.

name: BreakoutTestMeasuredMoveExpectation
quote: Whenever there is a perfect or near-perfect breakout test, the odds are high that the market will make about a measured move (expect the move up from the bar 12 low to be equal in points to the move from bars 6 to 9).

name: ReverseOnOppositeSignalInTightRangeWithRoom
quote: If you bought in a tight trading range in a bear trend and the market formed a low 2, you should exit and possibly reverse to short. If you shorted in that bear tight trading range and the market then formed a high 2, you should exit and possibly reverse to long, but only if the signal bar is a bull bar at the bottom of the range and there is enough room to the top of the pattern for a scalper's profit.
description: While long in a tight trading range, an opposite (Low 2) signal is grounds to exit and reverse to short; while short, an opposite (High 2) signal with a favorable signal bar is grounds to reverse to long, but only if there is enough remaining room within the range to reach a scalper's profit target.

hasRoomToTarget = (rangeHigh[0] - close[0]) >= minScalpTicks * tickSize; // room from here to the top of the range for a long reversal
enterLongNextBarOpen = ctx.MarketPosition() < 0 && isTightTradingRange[0] && isHigh2Setup[0] && isBullSignalBar[0] && hasRoomToTarget;
book_order_type: buy stop above the High 2 signal bar, closing the short and opening long

complexity.reason: reads position state (like FlatOrOpenLossExceeds) and composes the High2/Low2 pattern with a room-to-target measurement inside the tight-range regime

quote: exit 25 to 75 percent of your contracts at a scalper's profit that is equal to at least one to two times your initial risk, and then scale out of the remaining contracts as the market continues to go your way.

name: MinRewardToRiskAtSignalBar
quote: Almost all traders should only take trades where the reward is at least as large as the risk... the minimum starting point always should be a reward that is equal to the risk.
description: Pre-trade gate: use the signal bar's own range as a proxy for the planned risk (stop placed one tick beyond the bar) and require the planned points target to be at least a multiple of that range before taking the trade. Brooks ties the multiple to his subjective probability estimate (about 0.5x at 70%+ probability scalps, 1x at ~60% probability, 1.5x at ~50%, 2x at ~40% or less) but the probability itself cannot be read off OHLCV, so only the deterministic reward>=multiple*risk floor is mechanized here, defaulted to his most-repeated baseline of 1x ("reward at least as large as risk").
pseudocode: targetPoints >= rewardRiskMultiple * (high[0] - low[0])
book_order_type: n/a (pre-trade math check on the planned stop-entry/stop-exit, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic on high[0]/low[0] against two fixed parameters

notes: Brooks states four probability tiers with matching minimum reward:risk floors (page 171): ~70% prob -> 0.5x, ~60% -> 1x, ~50% -> 1.5x, ~40% or less -> 2x. Only the ratio test is mechanized; picking the tier requires the probability estimate itself, which is the research-grade R25-04.

Page 182 gives the same test concretely sized off the signal bar: 'the bar is six ticks tall, the stop will be eight ticks from the entry price, and they should use a profit target that is at least eight ticks away.'

Also discussed: commissions and slippage erode small scalps enough to flip a nominally-positive reward:risk gate negative (pages 177-178, 802-806); not mechanized separately since the book gives no fixed formula, only worked examples specific to instrument tick value.

name: ExitOnRewardRiskDeterioration
quote: If the trader's equation ever becomes marginal, he should try to exit quickly with as much profit as he can. If the trader's equation becomes negative, he should get out immediately, even if he ends up with a loss.
description: Position management: recompute the remaining reward (distance from the current close to the original planned target) and the remaining risk (distance from the current close down to the original planned stop) every bar, and exit once the remaining reward falls below a required multiple of the remaining risk -- the mechanizable half of Brooks's continuous re-evaluation of the trader's equation as price moves (dropping the probability term, which is not computable from bars).
pseudocode: remainingReward = (ctx.EntryPrice() + targetPoints) - close[0]; remainingRisk = close[0] - (ctx.EntryPrice() - stopPoints); remainingRisk > 0 && remainingReward < minRewardRiskMultiple * remainingRisk
book_order_type: discretionary early exit, no fixed order type in the book (traders exit at market or tighten and let the existing stop/target work)

complexity.reason: needs the position's entry price and the originally planned fixed target/stop distances as inputs, recomputed against the live close every bar

notes: Illustrated concretely on page 178-179 with a scalp example: 'raise their protective stops to one tick below the low of the current bar... this reduces the risk of the original trade to three ticks. They now might have an 80 percent chance of making the remaining two ticks while risking three ticks.'

Pairs naturally with R25-02 (a trailing stop shrinks remainingRisk over time, which keeps this test satisfied); the book does not separate the two, but they are independently mechanizable so kept split per the one-condition-per-candidate convention.
targetPoints/stopPoints reuse the same planned-trade parameters as R25-01; the authoring pass may want to share those inputs across a composite rather than duplicating them.

name: FixedTickScalpTargetWithFillSlippage

worstOpenProfitSinceEntry = ctx.MinPositionProfit(); requiredRiskDollars = -worstOpenProfitSinceEntry; profitTargetDollars = requiredRiskDollars - targetSlackDollars; exitLong = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= profitTargetDollars;

name: RetracementDepthRewardRiskGate
quote: Once a pullback rallies to above 50 percent, the chance of the bear resuming becomes less... Once the probability is 50 percent or less, traders will need more of a reward if they are going to short.
description: Size the minimum acceptable reward:risk ratio for a countertrend entry based on how deep the pullback has retraced into the prior swing: at a retracement of roughly 50% require at least a 1:1 reward:risk to the swing's test target, and at deeper retracements (around 61.8-67%) require at least 2:1.
